transcript:
Meeting: Redwood cost econ discovery with Ascend Capital
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rachel (Ascend - Head of ML), Tom (Infra Lead), Lena (CISO)

Summary: quick intro, customer goals (prod LLM features, budget constraints ~100k/year), detailed Q&A on per-token pricing and levers to reduce unit cost (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, route policies), security questions, and agreement on benchmark + pricing spreadsheet follow-up.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin — Ethan is our solutions engineer, he'll pair on the cost model discussion.
[00:15] Rachel (Ascend): Hi, Rachel here. we're building a customer support summarization and routing layer and evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. main constraint is budget — we're targeting ~= $100k annual for inference.
[00:28] Tom (Ascend): yes and infra team needs to know if we have to buy dedicated GPUs or if hosted will be cheaper.
[00:40] Ethan (Redwood): got it. high level — hosted is easiest to start, Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and better unit economics if you have steady traffic, and Private is for full control/compliance but usually higher up-front.
[00:55] Lena (Ascend): we also need SOC2 plus KMS and SSO — basically enterprise controls.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood): we cover SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated; hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys for many accounts, and we'll share the security pack.

[05:12] Rachel: ok for cost — can you give us concrete numbers? per-token or per-1k tokens so we can plug into our model.
[05:20] Ethan: sure, rough working numbers we discussed: Hosted generation ~ $0.05 / 1k tokens (combined prompt+completion), embeddings separately usually charged per vector but for your use-case it's generation. For Dedicated reserved pools, effective unit cost can drop to ~ $0.02 / 1k tokens depending on batch efficiency and commit level. Private/on-prem effective unit cost ranges more — often $0.01-0.03 per 1k tokens but that's very infra-dependent (GPU utilization, quantization, amortized infra).
[05:58] Tom: those deltas are useful. how much of that is just from batching? and what's the role of caching?
[06:06] Ethan: two big levers: batching across concurrent requests and KV/prefix caching. batching increases throughput on the GPU — you get better token/sec and lower cost per token because kernel startup amortizes. typical batch sizes we use are 8-32 depending on latency SLOs. caching — for chat or re-used context, KV cache and prefix cache can remove repeated computation; customers see 20-60% token reduction in practice, sometimes more for heavy prompt reuse.
[06:42] Rachel: so if our traffic pattern is many short chats with repeated system instructions, caching could be big.
[06:48] Ethan: exactly. plus we have smart routing and tiering so cold requests can go to hosted bursts and hot steady traffic to Dedicated. that hybrid helps keep costs under budget.

[09:00] Maya: quick note — quantization also matters. 8-bit quantization can reduce GPU memory footprint and let you run bigger batch sizes or cheaper GPUs. however quality tradeoffs vary by model; we'll recommend profiles per workload.

[12:15] Tom: can you explain committed capacity math? for example if we commit $15k/month for Dedicated, how do we translate that to tokens?
[12:24] Ethan: yes — dedicated pool pricing is: commit buys reserved GPU-hours and predictable throughput. the engineering team will run your prompt set against the config to estimate tokens/hour. ballpark: a $15k/month Dedicated commitment might map to ~600M generated tokens/month at 50% batching efficiency — but that's illustrative. we'll run a tailored benchmark and give a spreadsheet mapping tokens to cost under different batch/cache assumptions.

[15:40] Rachel: what about tail latency? batching helps cost but increases tail latency. our SLO is 300-500ms P95 for single-turn summarization.
[15:50] Ethan: right — there's always a trade-off. we can configure auto-scaling and smaller max batch sizes for low-latency routes. also prefix caching can maintain low latency for common contexts. in Dedicated you can pin lower-latency instances or set a latency-first policy at a slightly higher unit cost.

[18:30] Lena: security — if we go Hosted, can we use our own KMS? audit logs?
[18:38] Maya: yes, hosted supports customer KMS integration for encryption at rest for certain plans; for full audit controls and customer-managed network, Dedicated or Private offers deeper integrations. we'll attach the SOC2 and KMS doc.

[22:05] Tom: any gotchas on model variants? like smaller models cheaper but lower quality — how do you recommend choosing?
[22:13] Ethan: we recommend running a blind eval on your prompts. often a 7B quantized model with caching and batching can match quality needs at a fraction of cost versus a 70B. our Optimize tooling suggests model/quant profiles given quality thresholds. we'll include model recommendations in the spreadsheet.

[26:00] Rachel: for our $100k budget, what's realistic for production uptime and support? i.e., can we hit that with Hosted? Dedicated?
[26:09] Maya: short answer: Hosted can fit early-stage and bursty workloads; Dedicated is more economical for sustained production at scale. With $100k/yr (~$8.3k/mo) you could prototype on Hosted and then graduate to a small Dedicated commit as you approach steady traffic. Dedicated tends to require a larger monthly commit to be cost-effective. we'll model a 12-month ramp to show when the crossover happens.

[30:12] Ethan: suggested experiment — we'll run a 10k-request benchmark using your sample prompts across three configs: Hosted, Dedicated (small commit), and Private (if you want). we'll measure cost, P95 latency, and token savings with caching. that gives you the direct numbers to plug into the budget.

[33:40] Tom: about private deployment — besides infra cost, what's the support model and licensing?
[33:47] Maya: Private has an enterprise license plus a managed support fee; we also do onsite or remote assistance for onboarding. Private is best when strict data residency or air-gapped requirements exist. unit economics depend heavily on your GPU fleet and ops overhead.

[36:30] Rachel: curious — do you have customers in finance that did a similar cost analysis? any anonymized examples?
[36:36] Maya: yes, several funds and fintechs — anonymized case study we'll share showing Dedicated cut unit costs by ~50% vs hosted at scale after caching and quantization. details in the deck.

[39:10] Lena: can we get an ROI calc that includes engineering ops savings vs self-hosting? our infra team is leaning towards self-host because they think it will be cheaper long term.
[39:20] Ethan: absolutely — we'll include comparison of total cost of ownership: infra capex/opex plus ops headcount vs Redwood Dedicated/Private fees. note that our routing and autoscaling reduce ops burden and we include tooling for model rollouts and tracing which reduces MTTI.

[42:00] Maya: quick recap of agreements: Ascend to share sample prompts and qps profile by Monday; Redwood to run benchmark and send pricing + model recommendation spreadsheet; follow-up call to review results and discuss Dedicated sizing.
[42:20] Rachel: sounds good. thanks all.
[42:25] Tom: thanks.
[42:30] Lena: thanks.

[47:00] Maya: end call — we'll send calendar invite for the benchmark review.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors in proper nouns; some technical terms abbreviated. References: pricing deck (link shared in chat), benchmark plan (to be emailed).
